# Migrating from Appfire Flow (formerly Pluralsight Flow and GitPrime): the practical guide


Appfire Flow is shutting down, and every team that built dashboards, quarterly reviews, and reporting workflows on Flow, Pluralsight Flow, or GitPrime now has a real problem on a fixed deadline. This guide covers how to secure your historical data, evaluate Flow alternatives, and migrate to Waydev with your invoice matched and the migration done for you, free of charge.


[See your data in Waydev](https://waydev.co/demo/)


Summary


- Appfire Flow ceases operations in 2027. Export your historical data before your account closes.
- Every Flow capability has a direct Waydev equivalent: Git analytics, cycle time, DORA metrics, review workflow, and executive reporting.
- Waydev is Git-first, like Flow, and backed by a USPTO patent in Git analytics. It is the closest like-for-like replacement on the market.
- Waydev adds what Flow never had: AI adoption, impact, and ROI measurement across your engineering org.
- **For Flow customers: Waydev matches your current Flow invoice, and we handle the migration free of charge.**
- A four-week evaluation sprint gives you enough signal to make a confident decision.

## What to do before you evaluate any platform


Four decisions shape your evaluation more than any feature chart. Settle them before you take a single demo.


### 1.


Secure your historical data


Flow holds years of your engineering history: cycle time trends, review patterns, commit-level baselines. Export everything before your account closes. Then ask every vendor one question: can you ingest this, or do we start from zero?


### 2.


Map the processes built on top of Flow


The tool is not the problem. The workflows are. Weekly team reviews. Executive dashboards for the CTO. Automated stakeholder reports. List them all. You are replacing processes, not a login.


### 3.


Find your real deadline


Contract end is not your deadline. If leadership reviews engineering metrics monthly, your deadline is the next leadership meeting. If managers use the data weekly, it is sooner. Know what you are racing against.


### 4.


Know who signs off and what they care about


Your VP of Engineering wants proof at scale. Your CISO wants security documentation. Your CFO wants budget continuity. Your managers want zero disruption. Talk to them before you pick a winner, not after.


## How Waydev replaces what Flow provided


Waydev and Flow (formerly GitPrime) grew up in the same category: Git-native engineering analytics. Most platforms in this space are ticket-first. Waydev, like Flow, is Git-first. Your team’s mental model transfers directly.


Flow feature Waydev equivalent What you also get


**Commit-level Git analytics** ✓ Git analytics USPTO-patented. Work log, deep dive, repo-level views


**Cycle time tracking** ✓ Cycle time PR-level breakdown: coding, pickup, review, deploy


**DORA metrics** ✓ DORA metrics Benchmarks against industry baselines


**PR review analytics** ✓ Review workflow Review load, collaboration patterns, merge health


**Team activity reports** ✓ Team dashboards Configurable per team, role, or initiative


**Executive reporting** ✓ Reports & Goals Targets on any metric, tracked automatically


**Historical trend data** ✓ History rebuild History rebuilt directly from your Git provider


### No cold start: your history lives in Git


Your most important historical data is not locked inside Flow. It lives in your repositories. When Waydev connects to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps, it processes your full commit and PR history. Baselines, trends, and year-over-year comparisons rebuild from source. You do not start from zero. You start from day one of your Git history.


## What you gain by moving from Flow to Waydev


A forced migration is disruptive. It is also the moment to upgrade. Here is what Flow never gave you.


AI adoption / impact / ROI


### Answer the board’s AI question with data


Flow was built before AI-assisted development existed. It cannot tell you who is using Copilot, Cursor, or agentic tools, or what return the spend is generating. Waydev measures AI adoption, impact, and ROI across your org, tied to delivery outcomes, not seat counts.


Signals


### From dashboards to action


Metrics that sit in a dashboard change nothing. Waydev Signals runs AI-evaluated checks on your engineering work and sends findings straight to the people who can act, via Slack. Risky PRs, stalled work, review bottlenecks. Before the retro, not after.


Goals & AutoGoals


### Targets that track themselves


Set measurable targets on any metric. Cycle time under three days. Review pickup under four hours. Waydev tracks progress automatically. AutoGoals suggests realistic targets from your own baselines, so you are not guessing.


Roles & Anonymization


### Privacy-first measurement


Role-based access and anonymization controls give executives org-level visibility while protecting individual-level data. Works councils and legal teams have signed off on this model at enterprise scale, especially in Europe.


Vendor stability


### Bootstrapped, profitable, enterprise-proven


Waydev is profitable and bootstrapped, with Fortune 500 customers including American Express, Dropbox, Caterpillar, and PwC. No pressure to pivot, get acquired, or sunset the product. After Flow, stability is a feature. Ask every vendor about theirs.


## Running a focused four-week evaluation


You do not have six months for an RFP. You do not need it. Four weeks gives you enough signal to decide with confidence.


WEEK 1


### Shortlist and requirements


Pick two or three platforms based on your mapped processes and stakeholder concerns. Decline the rest.


WEEK 2


### Data-first demos


Ask each vendor to connect to a real repository and show your data in their platform. One ask, more signal than an hour of slides.


WEEK 3


### Migration clarity


Get specifics. Onboarding timeline. Historical data handling. Who owns the migration and what their SLA is.


WEEK 4


### Decision and business case


Choose. Use the memo template below to fast-track sign-off with your VP and finance stakeholders.


### The five criteria that matter in a forced migration


- **Data continuity:** do you keep your history or start from zero?
- **Time to first value:** how fast does the team see useful data after connecting?
- **Process coverage:** does it replace what Flow covered and the workflows built on top?
- **Migration support:** structured onboarding or figure-it-out-yourself?
- **Net gain:** is this a lateral move or an upgrade? Make it an upgrade.

## What are the alternatives to Flow?


Your inbox has been busy since the announcement. Everyone in this category knows Flow customers are shopping. Here is a candid brief, written in the same voice for every vendor, including Waydev at the end.


Platform Known for Where it falls short One question worth asking


**LinearB** Workflow automation (gitStream), strong marketing motion Automation-first, analytics second. Git-level depth is thinner than Flow’s. Show me commit-level work patterns for one of my teams, the way Flow did.

## Frequently asked questions


### When is Appfire Flow shutting down?


Appfire has announced that Flow (formerly Pluralsight Flow, originally GitPrime) will sunset in 2027. Your practical deadline is earlier: you need to be live on a Flow alternative before your final renewal, with time to export historical data and run both platforms in parallel. Confirm your exact end-of-support date with your Appfire account manager, then work backwards.


### What is the best Appfire Flow alternative?


It depends on why you chose Flow. If you picked it because it was Git-first, the closest architectural match is Waydev: Git-native engineering analytics backed by a USPTO patent, the same commit-and-PR-level lineage as GitPrime, plus AI adoption, impact, and ROI measurement Flow never had. Ticket-first platforms like Jellyfish and survey-first platforms like DX measure differently and will change how your reports work. The comparison section above covers the honest trade-offs.


### How long does migration from Flow to Waydev take?


Technical setup takes one to two weeks. Full rollout is typically complete within 30 to 60 days depending on org size. For Flow customers, Waydev’s team handles the migration free of charge.


### Can Waydev restore my historical trends?


Yes, and better than an import. Waydev rebuilds your history directly from your Git provider, so your baselines come from source data rather than a Flow export. Flow exports can supplement where useful.


### What does migrating to Waydev cost?


For Flow customers, Waydev matches your current Flow invoice, and migration services are free of charge: integrations, mapping, report recreation, and manager onboarding are handled by our team. In practice the budget conversation disappears, because the line item already exists and the price does not change.


### Is the budget already approved?


In most cases, yes. It was paying for Flow. Procurement moves faster when the alternative is having no platform at all. The memo template above is designed for exactly that conversation.


### What about security and compliance?


Waydev is SOC 2 certified and never stores your source code. Full security documentation is available for CISO review on request.


### How does Waydev measure AI impact?


Waydev tracks AI adoption, impact, and ROI across engineering, connecting AI tool usage to delivery outcomes at the PR level. You see who is adopting, whether output and quality are improving, and what the spend is returning.


### We measure engineers in Europe. Can we deploy this?


Yes. Role-based access and anonymization controls are built in. Individual-level data can be restricted or anonymized while leadership keeps org-level visibility.
